What is the TIC Pipeline?

The TIC (Taxonomy-Informed Clustering) pipeline groups amplicon sequence variants (ZOTUs) into biologically meaningful taxonomic units by using BOTH sequence similarity thresholds AND taxonomic classifications simultaneously.

Sequences sharing common taxonomy are clustered hierarchically at three biologically validated similarity thresholds:

  • Family level : 90% sequence similarity → FOTUs
  • Genus level : 95% sequence similarity → GOTUs
  • Species level : 98.7% sequence similarity → SOTUs (Species-level OTUs)

This prevents unrelated organisms that happen to share sequence similarity from being incorrectly merged, while accurately grouping true species variants.

Below is an explanation of each output file in this folder and how to use it.

1Primary Abundance Tables

Table
SOTUs-Table-TIC.tab
What it is
The primary abundance table for TIC mode. Each row represents a Species-level OTU (SOTU), columns represent your samples, and the final column provides the complete imputed taxonomy down to species level.
Use it for
This is the main data table for TIC analysis. Open it in Microsoft Excel, R, Python, or statistical packages for community composition analysis, diversity calculations, and biomarker discovery.
Table
SampleMinCount_Normalized-SOTUs-Table-TIC.tab
What it is
The SOTU abundance table normalized by subsampling (rarefying) every sample to the lowest sample sequencing depth.
Use it for
Unbiased alpha and beta diversity comparisons without sequencing depth artifacts.
Table
Spike_Normalized-SOTUs-Table-TIC.tabPresent only if spike-ins were used
What it is
The SOTU abundance table normalized using internal DNA spike-in standards.
Use it for
Absolute microbial abundance quantification (e.g., cell or copy numbers per gram/ml of sample).
Table
ZOTU-Table-OnlyBacteria-FullTaxonomy.tab
What it is
A high-resolution ZOTU table containing only validated bacterial sequences with full taxonomic annotations.
Use it for
Recommended for standard bacterial diversity and functional analyses (e.g., PICRUSt2). It excludes non-target amplicon noise, host mitochondrial/chloroplast contamination, and archaea.
Table
ZOTU-Table-All-FullTaxonomy.tabPresent if non-bacterial sequences were detected
What it is
A full ZOTU table containing all sequence variants, including bacteria, archaea, and unassigned/non-bacterial sequences.
Use it for
Quality control and broad-domain studies. Use this table if you want to quantify non-bacterial organisms (such as Archaea) or check what fraction of sequencing reads were non-bacterial or off-target. (Note: If no non-bacterial sequences are detected in your dataset, this table is identical to ZOTU-Table-OnlyBacteria-FullTaxonomy.tab and is automatically omitted to avoid redundant duplicate files).

2Representative Sequences & Quality Control

Sequences
SOTUs-Seqs-TIC.fasta
What it is
A standard FASTA file containing the representative (centroid) DNA sequence for each Species-level OTU (SOTU), with taxonomy in the headers.
Use it for
Sequence alignments, database queries (BLAST), and verifying representative sequences.
Sequences
Invalid-Tax-Seqs-TIC.fasta
What it is
A FASTA file containing sequences that failed taxonomic validation (e.g., non-bacterial reads, mitochondrial/chloroplast DNA, or sequences that could not be assigned valid 16S taxonomy).
Use it for
Quality control. Inspect this file to see which reads were filtered out and ensure your primers did not amplify off-target DNA.

3Hierarchical Mapping Tables

Mapping
Map-SOTU-ZOTU.tab
What it is
A mapping table showing which exact ZOTUs were clustered into each SOTU (Species-level OTU).
Use it for
Investigating within-species sequence diversity and tracking which sequence variants belong to which species cluster.
Mapping
Map-GOTU-SOTU.tab
What it is
A mapping table showing how SOTUs cluster into Genus-level OTUs (GOTUs, 95% similarity).
Use it for
Exploring genus-level groupings and relationships.
Mapping
Map-FOTU-GOTU.tab
What it is
A mapping table showing how Genus-level OTUs cluster into Family-level OTUs (FOTUs, 90% similarity).
Use it for
Exploring family-level groupings and relationships.

4Phylogenetic Trees

Tree
SOTUs-Tree-nj-TIC.tre
What it is
A phylogenetic tree of SOTU centroids in Newick format (.tre), built using Neighbor-Joining.
Use it for
Phylogeny-aware diversity calculations (UniFrac) in QIIME 2 or phyloseq, and visualization in tree viewers like FigTree or iTOL.

5Interactive Visualizations

Interactive
SOTUs-Krona.html
What it is
An interactive Krona taxonomy chart that opens in your browser.
Use it for
Double-click to view the taxonomic hierarchy of your SOTUs in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge.

6SILVA 144+ Dual Outputs (*-8Levels.*)

Generated when a reference database with bacterial kingdoms is used, e.g. SILVA >= 144

Table
SOTUs-Table-TIC-8Levels.tab
SOTUs-Seqs-TIC-8Levels.fasta
SOTUs-Krona-8Levels.html
Invalid-Tax-Seqs-TIC-8Levels.fasta
SampleMinCount_Normalized-SOTUs-Table-TIC-8Levels.tab
Spike_Normalized-SOTUs-Table-TIC-8Levels.tabIf spike-ins were used
What they are
The exact same TIC results as above, but with 8 taxonomic ranks including the bacterial Kingdom rank (e.g., Bacillati, Pseudomonadati).
Use them for
Use the *-8Levels files for the latest SILVA 144+ kingdom taxonomy, or use the standard files for tools requiring 7 levels.
